title: For more than 3,700 years, the Great Pyramid was the tallest thing people had built

cover.alt: The Great Pyramid of Giza, its stepped limestone core exposed, rising from the desert plateau under a clear blue sky.
cover.credit: Douwe C. van der Zee · CC BY-SA 4.0

body: Pharaoh Khufu’s pyramid at Giza was built around 2600 BC over about 26 years, from an estimated 2.3 million quarried blocks. When finished it stood **146.6 m** tall and was cased entirely in smooth white limestone; most of that casing has since been removed, and today it is 138.5 m. No human-made structure rose higher for more than 3,700 years. Its builders were also astonishingly exact: each side of the base is about 230.3 m long, and the four sides have an average error in length of only 58 mm.

slides.prompt: Each side of the base is about 230 m long. On average, how far off is each side’s length?
slides.detail: The base is also flat to within 21 mm, and the sides face the compass points to within an average of 3 minutes 38 seconds of arc.

slides.heading: 58 mm of error on a 230.3 m side
slides.note: Circle areas are to scale: the error is about 1/4,000 of the side.

left.label: When finished
left.text: 146.6 m tall, or 280 royal cubits, and cased entirely in smooth white limestone, its faces angled at 51°50′40″.

right.label: Today
right.text: 138.5 m tall. Most of the white casing has been removed, leaving the rough, stepped core you see now.

slides.heading: Who built it?
slides.text: Ancient Greek writers believed slaves built it, but discoveries at workers’ camps nearby suggest thousands of conscript labourers. In 2013 papyrus rolls called the Diary of Merer turned up at Wadi al-Jarf: a supervisor’s log of white limestone shipped from Tura to Giza in the 27th year of its pharaoh, Khufu.

slides.label: weight of the heaviest granite blocks, brought from Aswan more than 900 km to the south
slides.text: Granite pieces of 25 to 80 tonnes form the ceiling of the King’s Chamber and the relieving chambers above it.

slides.question: What does the Diary of Merer keep track of?
slides.explanation: It logs deliveries of white limestone from the Tura quarries to Giza, the stone used for the pyramid’s smooth outer casing.
